notes: One vague taste note. A good intake turns 'modern' into a short concrete list as its default reading (type scale, spacing, radius, colour) and asks the person to confirm or change it.
message:
## Brief

**Goal:** make the `proto-clinic` prototype (Northside Physio) look more modern, on the screens it already has. No new screens, no new features.

**Prototype:** `proto-clinic/index.html`. It is the only prototype in the folder, a single plain HTML file with four screens: Today, Clients, Invoices, Settings. No `package.json`, so I will run it with the loop's own small local server for plain HTML. Nothing is published, pushed, committed or sent; you get a local link only.

**Notes:** you gave one note, with no screenshots, no notes file, no reference and no `CLAUDE.md` in the folder. "More modern" is vague, so I turned it into concrete changes below. Each one is my reading, and you can correct any of them.

**Design rules:** no `product-design` or `design-review` skill is installed here, so I will follow the loop's built-in design check.

**Start check:** Node v25.9.0 is fine, and a browser for screenshots was found (Google Chrome). Before and after screenshots will work.

**Stop fact:** every row below is done and swept, no screen that no row names changed without a reason, and the prototype's link opens.

## Request list

| # | Note, in words | Screens | Where | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Softer, cleaner colour palette: near-white page background, one blue accent (a little deeper than today's `#2457d6`), lighter borders, and cards with a soft shadow instead of a hard outline (my reading) | all four | everywhere | `:root` colours and the `.card` shadow changed; text contrast stays at least 4.5:1; every screen still reads |
| 2 | Modern type: a system sans stack that starts with Inter, a clearer size scale (page titles 28px, table headers 12px uppercase with letter spacing) and lighter secondary text (my reading) | all four | everywhere | measured `font-size` of `h1` is 28px; table headers are uppercase on every table |
| 3 | Rounder, roomier shapes: card radius 14px, button radius 10px, input radius 10px, and more space between page sections (my reading) | all four | everywhere | measured `border-radius` and `gap` match on cards, buttons and inputs |
| 4 | Tables look like a modern list: more row height (about 14px of padding top and bottom, up from 4px), no lines between rows other than a faint one, a soft row highlight on hover, and the table sits inside a rounded card (my reading) | Today, Clients, Invoices | everywhere | measured `td` padding is 14px; a hover colour exists; the table is inside a rounded container |
| 5 | Navigation bar: the active tab becomes a filled soft-blue pill instead of the underline, tabs get a hover state, and the header gets a subtle blur or shadow (my reading) | all four | everywhere | `nav a.active` has a pill background and no underline; hover style exists |
| 6 | Buttons: add hover and pressed states and a keyboard focus ring; the "New appointment" and "Save changes" buttons keep their words (my reading) | Today, Settings | everywhere | `:hover` and `:focus-visible` rules exist on `.btn`; button text unchanged |
| 7 | Today's stat cards look like modern dashboard tiles: bigger number, small label above or below it, matching icon-free style (my reading) | Today | this place | the stat number measures 32px; the three tiles keep the same words and numbers |
| 8 | Status pills on Invoices: softer colours, a small dot before the word, same words as now (Paid, Sent) (my reading) | Invoices | this place | each pill has a dot; the words in `after/*.txt` match `before/*.txt` |
| 9 | Inputs and the select: taller (40px), a visible blue focus ring, a soft placeholder colour (my reading) | Clients, Invoices, Settings | everywhere | measured input `height` is 40px; a `:focus` ring rule exists |

I will not change any words on the screens, any sample data, or how anything behaves. While looking at the code I saw things that are not in your note: the "New appointment" button on Today does nothing, the Invoices "Overdue" filter shows an empty table with no words, the Clients menu item is titled "Customers" on its screen, and the Settings booking policy is placeholder Latin text. I will list these under "Broken before the run" and leave them exactly as they are, unless you add them as notes.

## Questions

1. **How far should "modern" go?** Default: **a polish, not a redesign.** Same layout and the same screens in the same order, with only colour, type, spacing and shapes changed. The other option is a bigger redesign, such as a left sidebar in place of the top bar.
2. **Do notes 1 to 6 and 9 apply to every screen?** Default: **yes, everywhere**, because they are about a kind of thing (colours, type, tables, buttons, inputs). Notes 7 and 8 are about one named element and stay on their own screen.
3. **Dark mode?** Default: **no.** One light theme only.
4. **Do you want a colour or a look to aim for?** Default: **a calm clinical blue and white, with Inter-style type.** Tell me a colour or a product you like if you have one.
5. **Anything that must not change?** Default: **nothing is protected**, and every screen may change only through a row above.

Notes you send later still join this run as new rows.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.

evidence.completeness: Settles modern (Q1 'a polish, not a redesign'), which screens (Q2 'yes, everywhere'), font/colour/spacing/radius (rows 1-3 with px values) and design rules ('follow the loop's built-in design check', Q4 look).
evidence.no_redundancy: States the prototype as a found fact ('It is the only prototype in the folder') instead of asking; no question repeats the ask or files.
evidence.defaults_quality: Every question has a concrete default fitting a clinic prototype, e.g. 'a calm clinical blue and white, with Inter-style type' and 'No. One light theme only.'
evidence.clarity: Five short one-topic questions with the key one first, but they sit under a long brief and a dense nine-row table that takes more than two minutes to read.
evidence.respects_words: Keeps to looks only ('I will not change any words on the screens, any sample data, or how anything behaves') and leaves the bugs it found alone; deeper accent and Inter are flagged as 'my reading'.
evidence.overall: A strong, faithful opening that settles scope and style with good defaults so 'go' works; held back only by its length.
